raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Fajita Marinade
raw_recipe.description: This easy-to-make chicken fajita marinade recipe will give your chicken the flavor you're looking for the next time you're making fajitas at home.
raw_recipe.name: Chicken Fajita Marinade

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk beer, lime juice, olive oil, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce, cilantro, cumin, and salt together in a bowl.

review.reviewBody: I have used this recipe for a couple years now and love it everytime! I have friends that have asked me for it as well. The only problem I have is using only a 1/4 cup of beer and then the rest gets wasted because I always start the marinade in the a.m. So, I have learned to make a large batch of the marinade. I freeze it with my chix breasts and also bags of cut-up peppers for my future fajitas. I just pull it out in the a.m. to thaw and it's ready to grill by the time I get home.

It was an awesome marinade!! I made it for a "Fiesta" last night and they were a big hit. The night before, I made the marinade exactly as the recipe stated and started to marinade the tenders in a ziploc, but then, quickly realized that the lime juice might actually cook my tenders or make them chewy while they hung out in the fridge. I rinsed out the tenders, kept the marinade, and re-marinated them 3 hours prior to the party. I also added a few dashes of liquid smoke, oregano, chili powder, & more cumin. I made a separate marinade for my veggie friends and marinated slices of green, red, and yellow bell peppers with sweet onions. The balance of the lime juice, garlic, & beer was perfect!! My husband cooked the veggies on an iron skillet on the grill and put the chicken on a flattop on the grill. I will definitely make these again. Thank-you reviewers for your modifications and Olivia for a great recipe!!

Very good recipe! I doubled the ingredients for the marinade. As I made this on a 25 below zero winter night in Chicago, I cooked the chicken indoors in a skillet. I added onions and green pepper strips and the marinade once the chicken was cooked thru. Boiled the marinade and cooked until the onions and pepper strips were cooked. Delicious!

DEEEELICIOUS!!! This recipe is perfect as is. No alterations are necessary, IMHO. Although my hubby wasn't as willing to give this a superb rating, he didn't have any "real" complaints either.... His only comment was that our fajitas were a little "limey," but that's what I like most about this recipe! I recently misplaced my go-to fajita recipe and am glad to have found a very similar replacement (and it's just as "limey"). :) After reading several reviews, I determined that my husband's opinion seems to be the dominant opinion on here also. Not wanting to cross-contaminate (i.e. marinating veggies w/ raw chicken), I made 2 batches of marinade - 1 for my cut-up chicken (I purchased a pkg. of tenderloins on sale) & another for my veggies (sliced Vadilla onion & red / green bell peppers). I marinated everything for 2 hrs. and used a sm. amount of the marinade (from veggies) to saute in, but I don't think the latter was necessary. I used Corona lite in my marinade w/ excellent results. For a fun presentaton, I preheated fajita pans (500 degree oven for ~ an hr.) to get a nice "sizzle" effect just like they do at authentic Mexican restaurants (or Chili's for that matter...). NOTE: The acidity of lime juice will break down (i.e. cook) your chicken. Two hrs. MAX is SPOT ON, allowing just enough time for the marinade to do it's magic. :) Served w/ Mexican Rice III (ALANSMOM), guac / chips & Mike's hard margaritas, this was an EXCELLENT meal! Thanks for sharing, Olivia! :-)

Great marinade. I rarely measure out exact amounts and it's always tasty. I use a full bottle of beer and probably a bit more oil and lime juice to help tenderize the meat and infuse the ingrediants. I will also typically marinate overnight and grill the next day. Chicken always comes out juicy and very flavorful.

This was fantastic! I used Michelob w/ lime for the beer and marinated the sliced chicken for just over an hour. Didn't grill- cooked in a saucepan with vegetable oil and leftover marinade. My husband LOVED this!

This recipe was a big hit tonight at dinner, and it was so easy to make. The family is on the P90X fitness/nutrition plan, and I wanted to surprise them with Chicken Fajitas!

I used thin-sliced chicken breast, placed them in a zip-lock bag with all the marinade ingredients (excluding the beer.) Then I sliced up strips of green & red peppers, but those in Ziploc steam bags. (easy & fat free instead of frying)and ready in just minutes. Marinated the chicken for close to 3 hours.

Served on "whole wheat" torillas, low-fat sour cream and fresh store bought salsa on the side, plus a homemade guacamole dip as well. Added a dish of Whole Wheat Tortilla Chips as well.

I got rave reviews from my husband & adult sons. They want me to make again and again....

Thank you for sharing this marinade recipe. I'll also try this recipe with steak fajita's for a change as well.

I felt so good tonite with all my family's compliments!

Delicioso! I didn't have beer but decided to substitute ginger ale. My husband also didn't like cilantro, so I substituted oregano, as suggested by another cook. I also used lemon juice instead of lime, because that was what I had on hand. I marinated the meat for 2 1/2 hours, removed carefully the chicken and seared on a grill pan. It smelled so good cooking! Then I used 1/2 of the bag of frozen red/yellow/green peppers (Trader Joe's) and sliced red onions. After cooking the chicken, I removed from the pan, added the vegetables and poured the marinade on them. Turned the grill pan on high for a few minutes, then lowered to medium-high for about 3 more minutes, added the chicken for a minute, then lowered the burner to low. Heated the soft tortillas and dished the mixture inside, sprinkled some sharp cheddar on top, wrapped and served. My husband said it was "superb!" I used 2 chicken breasts sliced into pieces. It made 5 medium wraps. Thanks so much Olivia. We loved it!

I didn't use beer or brown sugar because I didn't have them and this still turned out great! I made fajitas for a group of girls and they ate up every last bite! I even made a separate portion for a vegetarian friend and marinated the veggies - she left with the recipe!

We did shrimp and chicken but I only marinated the shrimp briefly to keep them from getting chewy. Yum, big hit with my 20 something kids. I used Corona and did use generous amounts of cumin and some chili powder bc we like some kick. These aren't a spicy variety but are flavorful none the less. Nice and tender. I also marinated the veggies in a seperate bag.

This was a great marinade except just a little too sweet. Next time I will definitely eliminate the brown sugar and add a little bit more lime. I also cooked my chicken and the vegetables in the marinade which tasted amazing.

I'm very pleased with this marinade and the taste! I made chicken fajitas but may have added a little too much lime (can you really have too much?), but this was the first time I've come close to restaurant taste, perhaps even better. Thank you and I will definitely use this again - maybe deluxe fajitas! I was only able to marinate for ~45 minutes but used the liquid to sauté the veggies.
I absolutely loved this marinade. Husband loved it as well. Great flavor and I made it exactly how the recipe is. We have used this marinade even when we're not making chicken fajita's.
I made these tonight. Honestly the least favorable fajitas I have ever had.
I made these tonight. Honestly the least favorable fajitas I have ever had.

I found this bland for my taste as written. I added extra cumin, some chili powder, and some tamarind powder (can get in Asian store) the tamarind gives it a little more tangy complexity. I also used garlic salt instead of regular salt. We loved it after those changes.
Love it! So yummy!

I've looked this recipe up so many times over the past several years I figured I should finally review it. It's definitely my go to for fajitas, and it freezes great too. I make this marinade and pour it over the chicken strips in a ziploc freezer bag and toss it into the freezer for a lazy dinner prep night. So great!
I didn't have lime juice but delicious! Quick and straight-forward!
This is my favorite marinade of all time!
